compareDisposition.rationale: The curator examined Pharaoh pursues Israel to the sea beside Israel crosses and the army is covered; Moses and Miriam lead songs by the sea. Those passages share its exodus evidence group or Scripture movement, but none supplies a distinct two-source relationship stronger than the accepted comparisons already carrying this topic.

observations.body: Israel turns back and camps between Migdol and the sea before Baal Zephon.
observations.label: A named encampment

observations.body: Pharaoh is expected to describe Israel as entangled and shut in; later he and his servants regret releasing them.
observations.label: Pharaoh’s reasoning

observations.body: Chosen chariots, Egypt’s other chariots, horsemen, and army overtake Israel at the sea.
observations.label: The force approaches

observations.body: Israel cries out and contrasts service in Egypt with death in the wilderness.
observations.label: The people speak

observations.body: Moses tells the people not to fear, to stand still, and to see what the LORD will do.
observations.label: Moses answers

payload.posture: Track the encampment, Pharaoh’s reasoning, pursuit, Israel’s fear and speech, and Moses’ answer before any path opens.
payload.tension: Israel has gone out with a high hand, yet the people now speak as though service in Egypt and death in the wilderness are their remaining alternatives.
payload.title: Between chariots and the sea
